Interface JournalSpi

All Superinterfaces:
Sweepable
All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractJournalSpi, CassandraJournalSpi, DynamoDbJournalSpi, HazelcastJournalSpi, InMemoryJournalSpi, MongoDbJournalSpi, NatsJournalSpi, PostgresJournalSpi, RabbitMqJournalSpi, RedisJournalSpi
public interface JournalSpi extends Sweepable
Backend SPI for Journal storage operations.

Implementations must provide ordered append, cursor-based reads, completion lifecycle management, and expiry semantics. The append and readAfter methods may be called concurrently from multiple threads. sweep may run concurrently with append.

  • Method Details

    • create

      void create(String key, Duration inactivityTtl)
      Create a new journal with an inactivity TTL. Must be atomic set-if-not-exists.
      Parameters:
      key - the backend storage key for the journal
      inactivityTtl - how long the journal may go without an append before it expires
      Throws:
      JournalAlreadyExistsException - if a live journal already exists at this key

    • append

      String append(String key, byte[] data, Duration entryTtl)
      Append an entry, resetting the journal's inactivity timer atomically.
      Parameters:
      key - the backend storage key for the journal
      data - the encoded entry payload
      entryTtl - how long this entry remains readable; Duration.ZERO stores it without a TTL
      Returns:
      the id of the appended entry, ordered after every id already in the journal
      Throws:
      JournalCompletedException - if the journal is completed
      JournalExpiredException - if the journal is expired

    • readAfter

      List<RawJournalEntry> readAfter(String key, String afterId)
      Read entries strictly after the given id.
      Parameters:
      key - the backend storage key for the journal
      afterId - the exclusive lower bound cursor
      Returns:
      the entries after the cursor in append order, empty if there are none
      Throws:
      JournalExpiredException - if the journal is expired

    • readLast

      List<RawJournalEntry> readLast(String key, int count)
      Read the last count entries in chronological order.
      Parameters:
      key - the backend storage key for the journal
      count - the maximum number of entries to return
      Returns:
      up to count of the most recent entries, oldest first
      Throws:
      JournalExpiredException - if the journal is expired

    • complete

      void complete(String key, Duration retentionTtl)
      Mark the journal as completed with a retention TTL. Calling on an already-completed journal updates the retention TTL (latest call wins).
      Parameters:
      key - the backend storage key for the journal
      retentionTtl - how long the completed journal stays readable; Duration.ZERO retains it without a TTL
      Throws:
      JournalExpiredException - if the journal is already expired

    • delete

      void delete(String key)
      Removes the journal and all of its entries. This operation is idempotent — deleting a non-existent journal is a no-op.
      Parameters:
      key - the backend storage key for the journal

    • exists

      boolean exists(String key)
      Returns whether a live journal exists at the given key.

      A journal is "live" if it was created and has not expired. Completed journals within their retention window still count as existing — they can be attached to and read, even though they no longer accept appends.

      Parameters:
      key - the backend storage key
      Returns:
      true if a live journal exists at this key

    • isComplete

      boolean isComplete(String key)
      Returns whether the journal has been marked as completed.
      Parameters:
      key - the backend storage key for the journal
      Returns:
      true if the journal has been completed; false otherwise
